subject: Careers
title: Customer service skills
lesson_success_checks: Use a calm invented request and the service brief to greet, listen/read, offer an allowed solution, explain a limit only if needed, and close. Try service worker and customer roles with usual access. Keep a service checklist, short reflection, five Week 1 expectation ratings and a next step.
source_assessment_summary: Formative review; staff confirm any later accredited mapping from actual evidence.
accreditation: The qualification/accredited unit, mapping confirmed by staff; no named scheme or awarding body.
calendar_note: Year A. Spring 1 Week 5, 1–5 February 2027. Friday 5 February 2027, P1. One forty-minute formative lesson for a pair. Six-week term 4 January–12 February; Week 6 assessing. No clock time supplied.
timing: Recall an expectation and a useful clarification phrase; agree access.
Model greeting, listening, solving, polite limits and closing.
Explore three calm scenes, rehearse checklist and private hinge.
Two six-minute role-play rounds; swap customer and service worker.
Short service reflection, five self-ratings, one next step/reply and save.

Business, order, roles, five expectation labels/meanings and four self-rating statements retained exactly. Reflection clue for finished work stays activity-neutral.

Friday 5 February P1, pair, forty minutes. Calm invented customer-service scenes: request, missing strip and request beyond the two-pack limit. Greet, listen, solve or seek help, say no politely only when needed, and close. Customer/service-worker role swap, five-item service checklist, short reflection and Week 1 expectations self-review. No real employer, product or place. Week 6 follows on acceptance; pause for Downloaded.

routes.Supported: Choose A, B or C. Keep the calm customer script, service brief, five-step guide and sentence starts visible. Use one phrase at a time, usual aid or exact scribe. Adult can partner. Swap roles and keep your own short service checklist, reflection and five ratings.
routes.Standard: Use the brief to respond to a calm invented customer, then swap roles. Check the request and offer a relevant fix or polite limit. Use the five-item service checklist with an actual example. Record a short reflection and rate the five Week 1 expectations.
routes.Stretch: Explain why a response fits the request and stays within the service brief. Improve one phrase so it gives a useful next step without an unsupported promise. Explain a limit of this short role-play. Swap roles and keep the same service checklist, reflection and five expectations; extra writing optional.

business.description: An invented small business prepares simple paper packs for customers. It has a supervisor, a preparer and a checker. It has no name, real employer, location or contact details. This is classroom simulation only.
business.order: Prepare two paper packs. Each pack needs one large card and one paper strip. Put the items beside each other. Check both packs against this order. Tell the checker when they are ready.
business.roles: The preparer arranges the materials. The checker reads the order and checks each pack. Agree roles, then swap after resetting the materials. An adult can take the other role if preferred.
business.limits: Use ready-cut paper only. No scissors, staplers, machines, food, money, customer data, live orders or deliveries. Accuracy, communication and support matter; speed is not assessed.

service_brief: In this invented practice, the service worker can offer two checked paper packs. Each pack has one large card beside one paper strip. A missing strip can be added and checked. A third pack is not available in this practice. Ask the supervisor about any extra request; do not promise an extra pack or a time. No money, real orders or customer details.

service_steps.label: Greet
service_steps.action: Welcome the customer in a clear, polite way.

service_steps.label: Listen
service_steps.action: Hear or read the request. Check what the customer needs.

service_steps.label: Solve
service_steps.action: Offer a simple allowed fix, or ask the supervisor for help.

service_steps.label: Say no politely
service_steps.action: If needed, explain the limit calmly and offer an allowed next step.

service_steps.label: Close
service_steps.action: Check what is agreed, thank the customer and close clearly.

scenarios.title: A simple request
scenarios.customer_line: Hello. Could I have two paper packs, please?
scenarios.worker_goal: Greet, check the request, offer two checked packs, confirm and thank. No refusal is needed.
scenarios.possible_response: Hello. You need two paper packs, is that right? I can offer two checked packs. Is that what you need? Thank you.

scenarios.title: A missing strip
scenarios.customer_line: Excuse me. One pack has no paper strip. Could you help, please?
scenarios.customer_reply: A strip and a check would help. Thank you.
scenarios.worker_goal: Acknowledge the mild complaint, check what is missing, offer one strip and check the pack. Confirm the fix and thank. No refusal is needed.
scenarios.possible_response: Thank you for telling me. I am sorry a strip is missing. Shall we check that pack? I can add one strip and check it. Is that now right? Thank you.

scenarios.title: One extra pack
scenarios.customer_line: Could I have a third paper pack now, please?
scenarios.customer_reply: I understand. Two is fine for now. Thank you.
scenarios.worker_goal: Greet and check the request. Explain the two-pack limit politely. Offer the two available packs or ask the supervisor about more without promising a result or time. Confirm and thank.
scenarios.possible_response: Hello. You would like three packs, is that right? I am sorry, I can offer two in this practice. I can ask the supervisor about more. Would the two available packs help? Thank you.

role_routine.service_worker: Greet, listen or read, check the request and use the service brief. Offer an allowed solution, say no politely only when needed, then confirm and close.
role_routine.customer: Use one calm invented customer line and the reply. No shouting, pressure, insults or acted anger. You can read, use an aid or select a line.
role_routine.swap: Choose one of the three scenes per round. Reset and swap customer and service worker for round two. Each learner records their actual worker turn and customer turn.
role_routine.access: Both can see the scripts and service brief. Use voice, usual aid, writing or selected words. An adult can partner. No public performance is required.

rounds.action: Choose a scene and roles, rehearse the calm exchange and record one service clue.
Reset and swap service worker and customer. Choose a scene, rehearse and keep each learner’s checklist.

service_checklist.label: Greeting
service_checklist.question: Was the customer welcomed clearly and politely?

service_checklist.label: Listening
service_checklist.question: Was the request heard or read and checked?

service_checklist.label: Simple solution
service_checklist.question: Was an allowed fix offered or help requested?

service_checklist.label: Polite limit
service_checklist.question: If needed, was a limit explained with a useful next step?

service_checklist.label: Closing
service_checklist.question: Was the agreement checked and the customer thanked?

service_checklist_scope: Use actual service-worker turn only. Polite limit is required in scene C; Not needed in this scene is valid for A and B. These service statuses are separate from the four Week 1 expectation ratings.
model: Invented scene C: a request for a third pack. The worker checks the request, explains that only two are available, offers those or a supervisor check without a promise, then confirms and thanks.
reflection_prompt: One thing I did to help the customer was…
reflection_alternatives: A phrase or aid that helped was…
I did not try this part yet; the help I need is…

expectations.label: Readiness and reliability
expectations.meaning: Know the agreed start and task. Get agreed materials ready. Tell the supervisor if a delay or support need affects the plan.
expectations.look_for: I checked the task and materials or asked for help to get ready.

expectations.label: Respectful communication
expectations.meaning: Listen or read, use respectful words and check meaning. You can ask for a pause or private help.
expectations.look_for: I listened or read and used a clear question or reply.

expectations.label: Instructions and quality
expectations.meaning: Check the steps. Ask if unsure. Check the finished work against the order before saying it is ready.
expectations.look_for: I checked a step or the finished packs against the order.

expectations.label: Safety and help
expectations.meaning: Keep the work area and access clear. Use only agreed materials. Stop and tell the supervisor if something is unsafe or unclear.
expectations.look_for: I kept the area clear or asked before doing an unclear task.

expectations.label: Teamwork and responsibility
expectations.meaning: Agree roles, share information and report mistakes honestly. Ask for a workable adjustment when needed.
expectations.look_for: I agreed a role, shared a useful update or reported a mistake.

reflection_prompts: I checked the task and materials or asked for help to get ready.
I listened or read and used a clear question or reply.
I checked a step or finished work against the instruction.
I kept the area clear or asked before doing an unclear task.
I agreed a role, shared a useful update or reported a mistake.
rating_states: I did this with a prompt
worked_examples_status: All worked examples, workplace, customer scenes and model exchanges are invented and declared. Record actual roles, customer request, response, support and reflection honestly. No real employer, person, product or place named.
private_help_route: Trusted adult or school help route. Point to HELP, write or ask privately. If one adult is busy, use the route to another. Pass, pause and supported return available. No personal customer, employment or family account requested.
typed_and_scribed_routes: Evidence Sheet pages 2–3: blank service task/reflection log and five-expectation review. Page 1 includes five blank service judgements and actual response clues. Book/voice/aid/typing/exact scribe valid; read back/correct. Record actual roles and any unobserved parts.
adaptations: Cognition and Learning: one short line/step, visible brief, checklist and reduced repetition. Communication and Interaction: rehearsal, wait time, usual aid, written or selected replies and exact scribe/readback. SEMH: predictable calm scripts, private review, pass and pause/return. Sensory and Physical: accessible table, seated turns and large print. EAL: plan in any language. 1 Point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 scaffold/choice; 5 model first step only then return task.
worked_example_and_fade: CfU after C model: no third pack is available in the practice. Offer two or ask supervisor about more without a promise or time. Keep scripts, brief and five-step guide; fade answer cues only. Usual communication/reading aid is access. A selected phrase or written exchange can show service thinking; a model or adult-supplied response is recorded as support.

main_hinge.claim: Explain the two-pack limit politely and offer an allowed next step without an unsupported promise.

parallel_hinge.claim: Check or clarify the customer request before offering a fix rather than guess.

assessment: Keep actual service worker/customer turns, chosen scene, response/result, five service checklist judgements with an actual clue, short reflection, five Week 1 self-ratings and one next step/reply. Service states: Seen; With a prompt; Not needed in this scene; Not seen yet. Polite limit may be Not needed in A/B; an unobserved opportunity is Not seen yet. Introduction/model of C does not prove an independent refusal. Week 1 ratings remain: I did this; I did this with a prompt; I need another try; Not seen today. Judge observable listening/checking, allowed response and clear closing; no eye-contact, smiling, appearance, fluency or personality criteria.

evidence.description: Individual actual customer/service-worker role record, five service judgements with actual clues, short service reflection, five expectation ratings, evidence clue and next step/reply.

where_this_leads: This helps me listen to a request, give clear honest information and ask for help while working with others.
colour_blind_safe: Numbered service steps, written scripts, labels and words carry meaning; no colour-only states.

paragraphs_in_document_order: Friday 5 February 2027 · P1 · 40 minutes · Year A
Careers · LAUNCH · a pair of learners · Spring 1 Week 5 · formative
Theme: Resilience & Change. Six-week term, 4 January–12 February; Week 6 assessing. Thread tags: SMSC So/M (S/C none); British Values MR/IL (D/RL/T none).
Source: LAUNCH Weekly - Spring row 92, B92 Spr1·W5 and C92 exact. Inherited framework/resource context from row 88 generic; no registration or award completion inferred.

Use a calm invented request and the service brief to greet, listen/read, offer an allowed solution, explain a limit only if needed, and close. Try service worker and customer roles with usual access. Keep a service checklist, short reflection, five Week 1 expectation ratings and a next step.

An invented small business prepares simple paper packs for customers. It has a supervisor, a preparer and a checker. It has no name, real employer, location or contact details. This is classroom simulation only.

Keep the Week 1 two-pack order and accurate checking. The worker uses the preparer/checker information to serve; the adult is supervisor and can partner. Week 4 clear questions and role swaps support this week. No real customer, employer, product or place.

Three calm scene cards, service brief, five-step guide, checklist, tier packs, vocabulary, book or blank Type instead and usual aids. Optional ready-cut paper packs illustrate the order; for B a card or prop can show one missing strip. Reset/reuse paper. No real orders, payment, contact or personal customer details. Confirm private help and adult partner route.
This helps me listen to a request, give clear honest information and ask for help while working with others.
Recall an expectation and a useful clarification phrase; agree access.
Model greeting, listening, solving, polite limits and closing.
Explore three calm scenes, rehearse checklist and private hinge.
Two six-minute role-play rounds; swap customer and service worker.
Short service reflection, five self-ratings, one next step/reply and save.
5 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 5 = 40 minutes. Source row 92 gives no minute sequence; these phases are authored. Processing and brief pauses included. Times guide the routine, not speed or performance style.

0–5: retrieve a Week 1 expectation and a useful clarification phrase from Week 4; agree access and roles. 5–9: explain five steps, with polite limits conditional. Read the service brief. 9–13: model invented C, a request for a third pack. Check request, explain only two available, offer those or ask supervisor without a result/time promise, confirm and thank. CfU: is a third pack available now? Key no; two or a supervisor check are the allowed next steps. Model is not learner evidence.

13–19: introduce all three calm scenes: A two packs, B mild missing-strip complaint, C third pack. Use customer lines and replies as written; no acted anger or added pressure. Compare relevant responses and practise the five-item checklist. A/B need no refusal; C uses a polite limit. 19–23: main hinge B honest two-pack limit and allowed next step rather than a third-pack/time promise. Parallel A clarify the request rather than guess. Re-model/recheck privately. Keep scripts and usual aids visible.

23–29 round one: choose A, B or C and roles. Rehearse one calm exchange, then record actual service clue and checklist. 29–35: reset, swap customer and service worker, choose a scene and repeat. Each learner gets a worker and customer opportunity; an adult can partner. Pause or reduce repeated talk for access; do not claim a planned turn occurred if not tried. Both can use voice, aid, writing or selected lines. No public performance, forced speech or memory test.

35–38: short individual reflection “One thing I did to help the customer was…” Or use: A phrase or aid that helped was… / I did not try this part yet; the help I need is… Rate the five Week 1 expectations from actual evidence. 38–40: privately check one clue, set one NS, keep reply and review time; save each record. Do not force a refusal to complete the checklist or request personal customer histories.

Choose A, B or C. Keep the calm customer script, service brief, five-step guide and sentence starts visible. Use one phrase at a time, usual aid or exact scribe. Adult can partner. Swap roles and keep your own short service checklist, reflection and five ratings.

Use the brief to respond to a calm invented customer, then swap roles. Check the request and offer a relevant fix or polite limit. Use the five-item service checklist with an actual example. Record a short reflection and rate the five Week 1 expectations.

Explain why a response fits the request and stays within the service brief. Improve one phrase so it gives a useful next step without an unsupported promise. Explain a limit of this short role-play. Swap roles and keep the same service checklist, reflection and five expectations; extra writing optional.

CfU after C model: no third pack is available in the practice. Offer two or ask supervisor about more without a promise or time. Keep scripts, brief and five-step guide; fade answer cues only. Usual communication/reading aid is access. A selected phrase or written exchange can show service thinking; a model or adult-supplied response is recorded as support.

Greet, listen or read, check the request and use the service brief. Offer an allowed solution, say no politely only when needed, then confirm and close. Use one calm invented customer line and the reply. No shouting, pressure, insults or acted anger. You can read, use an aid or select a line. Choose one of the three scenes per round. Reset and swap customer and service worker for round two. Each learner records their actual worker turn and customer turn. Both can see the scripts and service brief. Use voice, usual aid, writing or selected words. An adult can partner. No public performance is required.

Cognition and Learning: one short line/step, visible brief, checklist and reduced repetition. Communication and Interaction: rehearsal, wait time, usual aid, written or selected replies and exact scribe/readback. SEMH: predictable calm scripts, private review, pass and pause/return. Sensory and Physical: accessible table, seated turns and large print. EAL: plan in any language. 1 Point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 scaffold/choice; 5 model first step only then return task.

Trusted adult or school help route. Point to HELP, write or ask privately. If one adult is busy, use the route to another. Pass, pause and supported return available. No personal customer, employment or family account requested.

Evidence Sheet page 1 has five service checks with blank judgement and actual-clue cells. Page 2 is a blank typed service record, including scene, actual roles, response/result, service clue and short reflection. Page 3 has five blank Week 1 ratings and next step/help/reply. Page 4 is the private staff record. Book/usual aid default; all tiers use the same evidence goal.

Keep actual service worker/customer turns, chosen scene, response/result, five service checklist judgements with an actual clue, short reflection, five Week 1 self-ratings and one next step/reply. Service states: Seen; With a prompt; Not needed in this scene; Not seen yet. Polite limit may be Not needed in A/B; an unobserved opportunity is Not seen yet. Introduction/model of C does not prove an independent refusal. Week 1 ratings remain: I did this; I did this with a prompt; I need another try; Not seen today. Judge observable listening/checking, allowed response and clear closing; no eye-contact, smiling, appearance, fluency or personality criteria.

VF, WS, I, NS, //, ?, E and R generic codes. E actual banked work. R after Voice, Audience, NS and reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. One NS might check the request or replace a promise with a supervisor question. Retain first try and reply. Offer to Communication portfolio; staff confirm accredited mapping. A short classroom role-play does not prove workplace competence or real customer experience.

Calm invented lines only. No shouting, insults, acted anger or confrontation. No real orders, money, customer details, deliveries or unsafe tools. Optional ready-cut paper only. Keep clear/report actual concerns and follow school procedures. Listen calmly to concerns, avoid probing or secrecy promises and use the school route; keep private concerns outside shared evidence.
Only Week 5 authored. Week 6 work-experience reflection and half-term assessing follow one per return in the same invented business. Further GROW Careers paused.

Visible scripts/brief, usual aid, selected words or writing; adult can partner. Exact scribe reads back. No public performance, anger or personal customer history. Trusted adult/school route, pass/pause/return. No third-pack or time promise. Record missing opportunity honestly.
Use your book or normal aid. Optional Type instead cells are blank. Check your own actual service-worker turn, not the model or your partner’s work.

Was the request heard or read and checked?

For each: Seen; With a prompt; Not needed in this scene; Not seen yet. A polite limit is not needed in scene A or B. Do not invent a refusal. Use an actual phrase, action or aid as your clue.

Ask a trusted adult or use the school’s help route. Point to HELP, pass or pause. You can return with support. No personal customer history is needed.

Read exact scribing back. No refusal required in A/B. A pass is unobserved. E actual evidence saved; R after Voice, Audience, NS/reply. Offer to Communication portfolio. No real customer-service competence claim from role-play.
Calm task guides and invented examples, not learner observations.

In this invented practice, the service worker can offer two checked paper packs. Each pack has one large card beside one paper strip. A missing strip can be added and checked. A third pack is not available in this practice. Ask the supervisor about any extra request; do not promise an extra pack or a time. No money, real orders or customer details.

Service worker greets, checks need, offers an allowed response and closes. Customer reads/selects the calm line and reply without acted anger. Both keep scripts/brief/aids visible. Reset and swap for a worker and customer opportunity each. Adult can partner. No appearance, eye-contact, smiling or public-speaking test.

C model: “Hello. You would like three packs, is that right? I am sorry, I can offer two in this practice. I can ask the supervisor about more. Would the two available packs help? Thank you.” CfU key: a third pack is not available now; offer two or ask supervisor without promising a result or time. Main B honest limit plus allowed next step, rather than an extra pack or deadline promise. Parallel A clarify the request rather than guess. Re-model/recheck privately; pass unobserved.

23–29 round one; reset/swap and 29–35 round two. Choose one scene each round; all three introduced in We Do. Six minutes includes processing, calm exchange and short record. Reduce repeated talk for access. An introduced scene or adult model is not proof a learner performed that skill. Record actual role, scene, prompt and service clue.
Possible response only: “Hello. You need two paper packs, is that right? I can offer two checked packs. Is that what you need? Thank you.”
Greet, check the request, offer two checked packs, confirm and thank. No refusal is needed.
Possible response only: “Thank you for telling me. I am sorry a strip is missing. Shall we check that pack? I can add one strip and check it. Is that now right? Thank you.”
Acknowledge the mild complaint, check what is missing, offer one strip and check the pack. Confirm the fix and thank. No refusal is needed.

Possible response only: “Hello. You would like three packs, is that right? I am sorry, I can offer two in this practice. I can ask the supervisor about more. Would the two available packs help? Thank you.”
Greet and check the request. Explain the two-pack limit politely. Offer the two available packs or ask the supervisor about more without promising a result or time. Confirm and thank.

Greeting, Listening, Simple solution, Polite limit and Closing. Use Seen; With a prompt; Not needed in this scene; Not seen yet. In A/B refusal is not required; for the polite limit use Not needed in this scene. In C look for a calm two-pack limit and allowed next step without guarantee. Accept equivalent useful words, writing or aided selections within the brief. If a step was not observed, do not mark it Seen.

No pressure, threats, confrontation or escalation. The missing-strip complaint is mild; a strip can be added and checked. No third-pack/time promise. Do not require personal customer stories or emotional performance.

One thing I did to help the customer was… Possible only if it happened: “I checked that the customer needed two packs before offering them.”  Or use: A phrase or aid that helped was… / I did not try this part yet; the help I need is… Keep an actual clue. Do not treat the model as the learner’s response.
I checked the task and materials or asked for help to get ready.
I listened or read and used a clear question or reply.
I checked a step or finished work against the instruction.
I kept the area clear or asked before doing an unclear task.
I agreed a role, shared a useful update or reported a mistake.

Four Week 1 rating statements retained exactly: I did this; I did this with a prompt; I need another try; Not seen today. These are separate from the four service-check states. No total score or personality judgement.

Supported keeps brief, model, cards and phrase frames. Standard links a response to the request. Stretch explains an improvement and a limit of role-play. All retain usual aids, exact scribe/readback, adult partner and plan in any language. Private help/pause/return. Record access separately from content prompts. B92/C92 exact. Friday 5 February 2027 P1, pair, forty minutes formative; Week 6 assessing. Only Week 5 authored. Week 6 work-experience reflection follows after Downloaded. Same invented business; further GROW Careers paused.
Our invented workplace and service brief

An invented small business prepares simple paper packs for customers. It has a supervisor, a preparer and a checker. It has no name, real employer, location or contact details. This is classroom simulation only.

In this invented practice, the service worker can offer two checked paper packs. Each pack has one large card beside one paper strip. A missing strip can be added and checked. A third pack is not available in this practice. Ask the supervisor about any extra request; do not promise an extra pack or a time. No money, real orders or customer details.

Use a calm customer card and the service brief. One is customer, one service worker. Reset and swap so each has a turn. An adult can partner. Both keep scripts and usual aid visible; speaking, writing or selecting words are valid.
Use ready-cut paper only if props help. No real orders, customers, money, data or deliveries. Speed is not assessed.
All scenes are invented. Choose one per round. Use the customer line and reply without adding pressure or anger.
Customer: “Hello. Could I have two paper packs, please?”
Worker goal: Greet, check the request, offer two checked packs, confirm and thank. No refusal is needed.
Customer: “Excuse me. One pack has no paper strip. Could you help, please?”
Reply: “A strip and a check would help. Thank you.”
Worker goal: Acknowledge the mild complaint, check what is missing, offer one strip and check the pack. Confirm the fix and thank. No refusal is needed.
Customer: “Could I have a third paper pack now, please?”
Reply: “I understand. Two is fine for now. Thank you.”
Worker goal: Greet and check the request. Explain the two-pack limit politely. Offer the two available packs or ask the supervisor about more without promising a result or time. Confirm and thank.

Round one 23–29 minutes. Reset and swap customer/service worker for round two 29–35. Both see the brief and scripts. Use an aid, selected words, writing or adult partner. Times guide the routine; pause/reduce repeats for access. Record actual turns.
Welcome the customer in a clear, polite way.
Hear or read the request. Check what the customer needs.
